title: Quitting Hampton in New Orleans and staying on Bourbon Street
summary: Walked off at the Royal Orleans when Hampton played too long; returned to the Paddock.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: See, well, he had broken the big band out, he had a small band. He said, we'd like for you to play trumpet with the band. I said, okay, because I haven't been to New Orleans in a long time. I said, I'll go down there and see my, my, my relatives. So when we got there, the opening night, I quit the band. Because Lionel would get on the bandstand, he didn't know when to stop playing. He would just play, play, play, play. And the Dukes of Dixieland was supposed, we were scheduled to play too. We were supposed to play an hour, then the Dukes of Dixieland played an hour, then we played an hour, then we finished. But when Lionel got up there, after the Dukes played their hour, he ended up there and played about an hour and fifty minutes. About an hour and thirty minutes. So they tried to get him off the stage, he wouldn't get off the stage, he just kept playing. As long as he heard that, he was going to keep playing. So I'm at home, I got embarrassed, I just packed my horn up and left. Well he thought I was just going to leave for that show. But I left the band.

And then the word got on Burmett Street, my only trumpet player from New Orleans, he quit the band. So the people at the paddock whom I had worked for before, they sent for me, they said, I understand you quit the band. I said, yeah. They said, well what are you going to do now? I said, I'm going back to New York tomorrow. Why don't you come play with us again? I said, okay. So when I came in, I saw all these new buildings going up, these hotels and new highways and everything. I said, something big fixing to happen, I'll be able to stay here. And so I decided to stay here.
This must have been the late 60s. Yeah. Was Lionel always like this? I mean is that his playing for an audience?
